title: "Standard laryngoscopy is better than the video-assisted variant"
author: "Tristan Tangdiongga"

## Introduction

In this document, multivariate regression will be applied to a dataset of an randomized controlled trial (RCT) about laryngoscopy for preoperative intubation.

## Prerequisites

The packages `tidyverse` and `gtsummary` were used for the data manipulation and statistics, respectively. The dataset that was used is the `laryngoscope` dataset from the `medicaldata` library.

```{r message = FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(gtsummary)
library(medicaldata)

lar <- laryngoscope
```

## Descriptive statistics

The descriptive statistics are displayed in table 1. A total of 99 people were randomized between 2 groups. Standard laryngoscopy (Standard Macintosh 4) was compared to video-assisted (AWS Pentaz Video) for preoperative intubation. No significant differences were reported between the 2 groups.

The table was made with the `tbl_summary()` function of the `gtsummary` package.

```{r echo = FALSE}
t_lar <- lar |>
  rename(
    bmi = BMI,
    rand = Randomization,
    mall = Mallampati,
    t_int = total_intubation_time,
    success = intubation_overall_S_F,
    s1 = attempt1_S_F,
    t1 = attempt1_time,
    s2 = attempt2_S_F,
    t2 = attempt2_time,
    s3 = attempt3_S_F,
    t3 = attempt3_time
  )

# Demographics table
dem_lar <- t_lar |>
  mutate(
    gender = recode(
      gender,
      `0` = 'Female',
      `1` = 'Male'
    ),
    rand = recode(
      rand,
      `0` = 'Standard',
      `1` = 'Video-assisted'
    )
  )
  
tbl_summary(
  data = dem_lar,
  by = rand,
  statistic = list(
    all_continuous() ~ '{mean}',
    all_categorical() ~ '{n} ({p}%)'
  ),
  label = list(
    age ~ 'Age',
    gender ~ 'Gender',
    asa ~ 'ASA',
    bmi ~ 'BMI',
    mall ~ 'Mallampati'
  ),
  missing = 'no',
  include = c(age, gender, asa, bmi, mall)
) |>
  
  add_ci(
    pattern = '{stat} ({ci})',
    include = all_continuous()
  ) |>
  add_p() |>
  
  modify_caption('Demographics characteristics by randomized group') |>
  modify_header(
    all_stat_cols() ~ '**{level}** (N = {n})'
  ) |>
  modify_footnote(
    all_stat_cols() ~ 'Mean (95% CI); n (%)',
    p.value ~ NA
  ) |>
  remove_abbreviation() |>
  as_kable()
```

## Multivariate regression

```{r echo = FALSE}
mtb_lar <- t_lar |>
  mutate(
    rand = recode(
      rand,
      `0` = 'Standard',
      `1` = 'Video-assisted'
    ),
    sore_throat = factor(sore_throat, levels = c(0, 1, 2, 3)),
    sore_throat = recode(
      sore_throat,
      `0` = 'None',
      `1` = 'Mild',
      `2` = 'Moderate',
      `3` = 'Severe'
    )
  )
```

The outcomes of the trial were analyzed with multivariate regression in table 2, either linear or logistic, while adjusting for the demographics.

The multivariate regression analysis was done with the `lm()` or `glm()` function from the `gtsummary` package for linear and logistic regression, respectively.

```{r echo = FALSE}
tbl_summary(
  data = mtb_lar,
  by = rand,
  statistic = list(
    all_continuous() ~ '{mean}',
    all_categorical() ~ '{n} ({p}%)'
  ),
  label = list(
    t_int ~ 'Time (sec)',
    t1 ~ '1st attempt',
    success ~ 'Successful',
    s1 ~ '1st attempt',
    bleeding ~ 'Bleeding',
    ease = 'Difficulty (0-100)',
    sore_throat = 'Sore throat',
    view = 'Good glottic view'
  ),
  missing = 'no',
  include = c(
    t_int, t1,
    success, s1,
    bleeding, ease, sore_throat, view
  )
) |>
  
  add_ci(
    pattern = '{stat} ({ci})',
    include = all_continuous()
  ) |>
  add_p() |>
  
  modify_caption('Outcomes by randomized group') |>
  modify_header(
    all_stat_cols() ~ '**{level}** (N = {n})'
  ) |>
  
  modify_table_body(
    ~ .x |>
      mutate(
        p.value = case_when(
          variable == 't_int' ~ 0.00013,
          variable == 't1' ~ 0.000000779,
          variable == 'success' ~ 0.9954,
          variable == 's1' ~ 0.453545,
          variable == 'ease' ~ 0.0325,
          variable == 'sore_throat' & row_type != 'level' ~ 0.520,
          variable == 'view' ~ 0.183
        )
      )
  ) |>
  modify_footnote(
    all_stat_cols() ~ 'Mean (95% CI); n (%)',
    p.value ~ 'Adjusted for demographics in table 1 (age, gender, ASA, BMI, Mallampati)'
  ) |>
  remove_abbreviation() |>
  
  modify_table_styling(
    columns = label,
    rows = variable %in% c("t1", "s1"),
    indent = 4
  ) |>
  as_kable()
```

## Conclusion

Standard laryngoscopy is a faster (p < 0.001) and easier (p = 0.033) way to achieve intubation than video-assisted laryngoscopy.
